text:
Ana Romero: quick design review pls — new staged-release panel mock in figma. major asks: split-test labeling, rollback affordance, and screen-reader announce for historical scrubber. cc @Mike Chen and @Jon Park
Mike Chen: saw the fig — overall nice. one nit: the split-test variants use full names, takes too much horizontal space when you have 6 variants. can we abbreviate? e.g., `v1-small`, `v2-large` instead of the long model keys? :thinking_face:
Shweta Patel: +1 on shorter labels. also we need explicit tooltip copy for what each variant means (traffic, model size, quantization). product wants non-technical fallback copy for PMs.
Ana Romero: idea: show compact label + hover tooltip with full model id and a small badge line for meta (region | q4bit | latency tier). will that break keyboard nav?
Mike Chen: keyboard nav unaffected if we make the variant a single focusable element. but we should avoid putting the tooltip content inside a focus trap. for keyboard users, show an inline expandable row on Enter instead of a hover-only tooltip.
Jon Park: a11y: screen reader users need clear context when scrubber moves through timeline. 2 things: announce date/version and whether that checkpoint had a rollback or canary. use `aria-live="polite"` for incremental changes, but set `aria-atomic` and include a short prefix like "History:"
Ana Romero: can you draft the exact aria text we should emit? aiming for short phrases.
Jon Park: suggestion examples: 
``` 
"History: March 12, 2026 — staged release 20% to variant A — no rollback"
"History: March 11, 2026 — reverted to v3.1.2 after rollback"
``` 
Jon Park: also recommend adding a visually-hidden status icon with text (e.g., "rolled back", "active canary") for screen readers, separate from the timeline label.
Design Bot: automated visual regression: timeline-compact-variants bumped contrast for the active pill to 4.6:1 — passed.
Shweta Patel: copy tweak request: change CTA from "Rollback" to "Revert to previous" in the confirm dialog — legal prefers clearer wording. UX prefers shorter though. thoughts?
Mike Chen: "Revert to previous" is clearer in modal but in the action menu I'd keep "Rollback" as the verb — shorter in a tight menu. we can have the modal title: "Confirm revert to previous version" and primary button: "Revert".
Ana Romero: agree with Mike. will update designs to show both: action menu uses "Rollback" with an icon, modal shows full phrase.
Jon Park: keyboard + SR check for the modal: ensure focus lands on primary button and `role="alertdialog"` with accessible name. also include a brief reason field for auditors (optional).
Shweta Patel: auditors will ❤️ the reason field. product asks: store the reason in rollout history so ops can filter by "rollback reason".
Ana Romero: good call — adding a small metadata column in the timeline for "note" (truncated) with full text in flyout.
Mike Chen: tiny CSS/spacing nit: the variant badges in compact mode look cramped at 320px. please ensure min touch target 44px for touch screens.
Ana Romero: noted — will add min height and update responsive breakpoints.
Shweta Patel: final blocker: A/B split percentages slider — are we allowing fractional percentages (0.5%)? infra limits to integer %s for now. need copy that matches constraint.
Mike Chen: backend only supports whole ints today. UI should validate and show helper text: "Traffic allocation accepts whole percentages only." and prevent decimal input.
Ana Romero: ok I'll add helper text and disable decimal step in the input.
Jon Park: last a11y note: when the allocation changes, announce delta: "Allocation changed: variant A +5%" so SR users understand the change. use `aria-live` region and a short verb phrase.
Ana Romero: perfect — thanks all. I'll upload updated figma frames and tag you when done. https://www.figma.com/file/xyz/staged-release-panel
DeployBot: deploy-preview succeeded for branch `staged-release-ui` at sha abc123 — preview link: https://preview.redwood.dev/staged-release-ui
Mike Chen: preview looks good on chrome, will test Safari today. :+1:
